Vector microprocessors

reception: Citers treat the article less as an argument than as a handle for the SUIF parallelizer: most substantive citations come from work that uses the system. SUIF Explorer and compiler-directed page coloring build on the infrastructure within the Stanford orbit, a long line of embedded-systems and energy-optimization studies by Kandemir and colleagues cites the article for the compiler their experiments run on, and hardware/software co-compilation efforts from FPGA module mapping to the Nymble system do the same. The article's own thesis — that architects should design for parallelizing compilers — draws less direct engagement, surviving mainly in occasional passing references.
